sites.name: Hoa Binh Hydropower Plant
sites.event: The monumental work of the century conquering the Da River, a symbol of industrialization and Vietnam-Soviet friendship, where the Letter of the Century to future generations is kept.

sites.name: Thung Nai (Hoa Binh Lake)
sites.event: Likened to 'Ha Long Bay on land' with hundreds of small islands floating on the blue water of the Da River reservoir.

sites.name: Lac Village
sites.event: A more than 700-year-old ancient village of the White Thai people, the cradle of community-based tourism in Vietnam.

sites.name: Thung Khe Pass (White Stone Pass)
sites.event: Famous for its snow-white landscape caused by limestone landslides and the roadside Muong ethnic market.

sites.name: Kim Boi Hot Spring
sites.event: An open-air natural mineral water source with the lowest temperature in Vietnam (34-36 degrees Celsius), containing many health-beneficial minerals.

sites.name: Thac Bo Temple (Temple of the Goddess of Thac Bo)
sites.event: The place of worship for Mrs. Dinh Thi Van and Mrs. Quach Thi Lan, two female generals who helped King Le Loi suppress rebellions and control the Da River waters.

place.commune: Thung Nai Commune, Vay Nua Commune
place.district: Cao Phong District, Da Bac District

sites.name: Dong Thech Ancient Tombs Relic Site
sites.event: The burial site of the Dinh clan (Muong lords) over many centuries, harboring mysteries about the culture and beliefs of the ancient Muong people.

sites.name: Xom Trai Cave
sites.event: The most typical archaeological relic of the Hoa Binh Culture (Stone Age), proving the existence of prehistoric humans tens of thousands of years ago.

sites.name: Ba Khan Valley
sites.event: A peaceful valley located between Mai Chau and the Da River reservoir, likened to a 'forgotten paradise'.

sites.name: Tu Son Nine Waterfalls
sites.event: A majestic scenic spot with 9 consecutive waterfalls, associated with the love story of the Fairy youth and Lady Ngoc.

sites.name: Phu Canh Nature Reserve
sites.event: A primeval forest preserving a diverse ecosystem and the culture of the Muong and Dao ethnic groups in the reservoir area.
